### Historical audit: S0019

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v2_2/results/r1/fixed_h/r1_C2/fixed_version_test/commons_104864364/trajectory.jsonl`. Only chunk 1 of 2 is visible; the reference and rendered images themselves are not visible to this audit.

| Evidence | Observation and limit |
|---|---|
| Student `model_request`, line 1 | The assigned goal was a separate-mesh reconstruction of a single indoor RGB view, including camera and framing, under two executions. The classroom interpretation below is the student’s inventory, not independent image identification. |
| Student `model_response`, line 3; `execute`, line 4 | The first complete program constructed multiple named assets: room, openings, stage, desks and benches, bags, books, fans and pictures. It grouped desk legs and shelves, bag pockets and straps, and fan blades under assets; grouping does not verify physical connections or visual correctness. It specified an upright room arrangement, fan rotations, a camera, three lights, colors and an attempted procedural floor texture. |
| `execution_result`, line 5, characters [0,58528); `select`, line 6 | Step 1 reported `ok: true`, saved a render and blend file in 23.67 seconds, and was selected. This establishes technical execution, not image fidelity. |
| Student `model_request`, line 7, characters [0,82867); `model_response`, line 9 | The student was given the first render and asked to compare it with the reference. Its own feedback claimed pale furniture, displaced foreground desks, a low stage header and absent floor tiles, attributing the last issue to generic realized mesh names. These are student detections and a diagnosis, not independently verified findings. |
| Student `model_response`, line 9; `execute`, line 10 | The executed revision darkened materials and lighting, moved and added desk rows, raised stage elements, reshaped and repositioned bags, and changed floor selection from part name to dimensions. The camera parameters stayed unchanged. These are actual code changes, not proof that the claimed defects were fixed. |
| `execution_result`, line 11, characters [0,63241); `select`, line 12 | Step 2 reported `ok: true`, saved a render and blend file in 29.92 seconds, and was selected. No visible comparison of that render or final formal correctness assessment appears in this chunk. |

**Input and exploration.** The visible guidance came from the task system and runner: the latter supplied the render and requested comparison or `DONE`. No separate teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or student receipt of teacher feedback is visible. The revision is student-authored; the two recorded student sessions report zero tool calls (lines 2 and 8). The two builds and the student’s comparison are the visible exploration, not evidence of additional unseen experiments.

**Outcome and uncertainty.** Both builds technically succeeded; overall reconstruction correctness is **unknown**, not formally successful or demonstrably failed. In particular, object coverage, relative pose and placement, part contact, texture application, camera framing, lighting and any render artifacts cannot be verified without seeing the images. Whether geometry-based floor selection actually applied the intended material remains unresolved. The student also explicitly marked occluded furniture and stage depth uncertain.

**Lessons.** Transferably, execution success and an editable hierarchy are weaker evidence than a rendered comparison; a diagnosis should remain separate from its attempted repair. The floor-name hypothesis and the particular desk, stage and lighting adjustments are task-specific and remain visually unverified.
